chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Kindness is not placed upon anything except that it adorns it, and it is not removed from anything except that it dishonours it.'

key_terms.الرِّفْقَ: Kindness, gentleness, or ease in conduct
key_terms.شَانَهُ: It dishonours or diminishes its status

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of kindness on character and actions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the reliable chain of Zurara, this Prophetic tradition underscores الرفق (gentleness) as an essential aesthetic and spiritual virtue that perfects all matters. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to mean that kindness is not merely a moral choice but a divine attribute that elevates the intrinsic value of actions, relationships, and even physical objects, while harshness detracts from their nobility.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The kindness is such that it does not get placed upon anything except that it adorns it, and it is not removed from anything except it dishonours that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhayna from Zurara from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
There is nothing in which friendliness is placed but that such thing is beautified. There is nothing from which friendliness is removed but that such thing is shunned.”’
